intro.data: Every functor has an identity transformation that changes nothing. Here F and G are both List. One candidate keeps each list as-is; the other pads in a default and is not natural. Build the identity transformation.
intro.alchemy: Every functor has an identity transformation that changes nothing. Here F and G are both Batch. One candidate keeps each batch as-is; the other pads in a spare and is not natural. Build the identity transformation.
intro.spellcraft: Every functor has an identity transformation that changes nothing. Here F and G are both Swarm. One candidate keeps each swarm as-is; the other conjures an extra and is not natural. Build the identity transformation.
intro.abstract: When F = G, the identity transformation id_F has component id at every object. One distractor is typed right but not natural. Build id_F.

goal.data: Pick the keep-as-is (identity) component at each object.
goal.alchemy: Pick the keep-as-is (identity) component at each material.
goal.spellcraft: Pick the keep-as-is (identity) component at each essence.
goal.abstract: Pick the identity component at each object.

afterSuccess.data: The identity component at every object gives the identity transformation id_F — it does nothing and trivially commutes. padDefault is typed right but breaks the square. id_F is the identity arrow of the functor category [C, D].
afterSuccess.alchemy: The keep component at every material gives the identity transformation id_F — it does nothing and trivially commutes. The spare-adding one breaks the square.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The keep component at every essence gives the identity transformation id_F — it does nothing and trivially commutes. The conjuring one breaks the square.
afterSuccess.abstract: Identity components everywhere give id_F : F ⇒ F, the identity of the functor category [C, D]. The padding family is typed right but not natural.

reveal.summary: For any functor F there is an identity natural transformation id_F : F ⇒ F (the identity component at each object). It is the identity morphism in the functor category [C, D].
reveal.moreFormal: Functor categories [C, D] have functors as objects and natural transformations as morphisms, composed component-wise. id_F is each object's identity — the unit of that composition (a future chapter).
reveal.programmerAnalogy: The identity polymorphic function id<A>: F<A> => F<A> — changes nothing, natural everywhere.
